newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures dragged lower with NYMEX selling.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures dragged lower with NYMEX selling.

text.p: IPE Brent futures eased on Monday, following early selling on the NYMEX which took the London front month contract to a session low of $17.61 a barrel, brokers said.
By 1450 GMT, prompt July Brent was down one cent at $17.69 a barrel.

"We're a little bit dominated by what's going on in the (United) States," one broker said. "There was good buying towards the lows at the New York opening and some of the locals went long, but it hasn't rallied too far. It looks as though some of the locals are trying to get out now."
The market here took its lead from a softer U.S. crude and from NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures, which led the downtrend.
IPE gas oil, meanwhile, was catching up on Brent's Friday sell-off, but the June contract was also under pressure from the softer tone in the U.S.
By 1430 the contract was at $160.50, off $3.50 a tonne.

Brent took its cue from the U.S. market on Friday, where prompt crude fell to its lowest level in 16 months as commodity funds baled out amid evidence of slack gasoline demand, rising crude inventories and record refinery production.
Renewal of the United Nations oil-for-food deal with Iraq, allowing Baghdad to sell another $2 billion worth of oil over the next six months, also gave speculators an excuse to sell-off.
